articles.headline: Kisangani : 17 déplacés morts de faim et de maladies sur le site de
articles.headlineTranslated: Kisangani: 17 displaced people died of hunger and disease on the site of.
articles.summary: At the Konga-Konga displacement site in Kisangani, Tshopo, 17 people have died since the start of 2026 from hunger and lack of medical care amid clashes between Mbole and Lengola communities. Local authorities warn the humanitarian situation is dramatic; the last emergency aid arrived on 3 January, leaving displaced residents in extreme precarity. The municipal mayor, Jupson Bokendi Popolipo, reports the health center at the site lacks medicines, and after MSF interventions to contain a cholera outbreak, local facilities can no longer treat patients. "We have recorded seventeen deaths from various diseases... there are no medicines," he said. Between 3,000 and 4,000 children leave the site daily to beg in Kisangani, highlighting severe food insecurity. The mayor appeals for urgent provincial, national, and humanitarian action to address the crisis.

articles.headline: Биолог рассказал о новых клещах-гигантах на юге России
articles.headlineTranslated: Biologist spoke about new giant ticks in southern Russia.
articles.summary: Southern Russia reports appearance of giant Hyalomma ticks now actively pursuing humans by scent and heat. These ticks, described as mutant/giant, differ from ordinary ticks that wait in vegetation. Hyalomma has historically inhabited Africa and Asia and has spread to southern Russia as winters warm, allowing survival. The ticks are vectors for Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus, a disease with mortality reported up to 30-40%. Early symptoms resemble influenza (fever, headache) and can progress to internal bleeding and seizures. The article provides no human case counts or laboratory confirmation details. It notes that common insect repellents are largely ineffective due to resistance, recommending mechanical protection (protective clothing, barriers). The report references Sun findings of European spread. Published 2026-03-19.

articles.headline: Fallecen 484 personas por cólera en África desde enero de 2026
articles.headlineTranslated: 484 people have died from cholera in Africa since January 2026.
articles.summary: Cholera remains a major public health concern in Africa, where 484 deaths have occurred since January 2026, amid nearly 18,500 suspected and 5,300 confirmed cases. Africa accounts for about 59% of global cholera cases, with a case fatality rate of 2.03%. The Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, and Nigeria are among the most affected countries. The African Union's health agency and Africa CDC are monitoring Sudan after declaring the end of its outbreak on March 5 to prevent resurgence, as observed in Rwanda and Zimbabwe. Officials are tracking lessons learned to advance the continent's Cholera Elimination Plan for 2030. Fourteen member states have reported cases this year, underscoring the ongoing outbreak and the need for sustained surveillance and public health measures.

articles.headlineTranslated: At least 484 people have died of cholera in Africa this year
articles.summary: Cholera outbreaks in Africa: as of 19 March 2026, at least 484 deaths and 14 countries reporting cases, representing 59% of global cholera cases; case fatality rate 2.03%. Affected: Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, Nigeria; Sudan monitored after 5 March end of outbreak to prevent resurgence like Rwanda and Zimbabwe. Africa last year had about 262,300 cases and 5,900 deaths, a record high. Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae, contracted via contaminated food or water, linked to poor sanitation and limited access to potable water. It is treatable; fatalities can occur without prompt care. Africa CDC aims to support post-outbreak assessment and inform continent-wide cholera elimination by 2030.

articles.headline: Detectan la cepa más peligrosa de viruela del mono en la Argentina y un hombre está internado
articles.headlineTranslated: The most dangerous strain of monkeypox detected in Argentina and a man is hospitalized.
articles.summary: Argentina detects monkeypox clade Ib, originating in DR Congo in 2023, a shift from earlier clade II cases in the country. Clade Ib is linked to greater severity and contagiousness. The outbreak has spread to the United States, Canada, Brazil and Mexico, with community transmission in Spain, France and Portugal. Symptoms include skin lesions (pink spots, ulcers, vesicles, or crusts) often near the genitals or face; fever, malaise, severe headache; painful lymphadenopathy; proctitis and sore throat. Incubation is 6–13 days, up to 21; more severe in immunosuppressed individuals or those with uncontrolled HIV. Health authorities recommend intensified surveillance and high suspicion for sudden rash; immediate medical evaluation; isolation until crusts fall and new skin forms; contact tracing within 24 hours. WHO vaccines exist for select groups, but Argentina prioritizes early detection and symptom management to prevent complications like bacterial infections or sepsis; Mendoza had earlier cases.

articles.headline: Assemblée nationale : Joseph Nkoy interpelle le ministre de la Justice sur le choléra dans les cachots - LePotentiel
articles.headlineTranslated: National Assembly: Joseph Nkoy questions the Minister of Justice about cholera in the dungeons - Le Potentiel
articles.summary: Cholera in detention facilities in the Democratic Republic of Congo prompts 80 written and oral questions in the National Assembly's March session. National MP Joseph Nkoy submitted an oral question with debate to Justice Minister Guillaume Ngefa Atondoko seeking details on measures to combat cholera in overcrowded dungeons, amid concerns over prisoners’ detention conditions. The minister recently conducted an inspection tour; Nkoy asks for conclusions and links to the decision to ban transferring detainees to CPRK to curb spread of cholera caused by overcrowding. He also questions whether concrete steps have been taken to resolve the problem in the dungeons and in detention places described as 'amigos.' Observers note Makala Central Prison houses more preventive detainees than convicted inmates, highlighting overcrowding as a driver of infection risk.

articles.headline: Malnutrition, paludisme et maladies infectieuses : des millions d'enfants en meurent avant 5 ans
articles.headlineTranslated: Malnutrition, malaria and infectious diseases: millions of children die from them before the age of five.
articles.summary: In 2024, about 4.9 million children under five died worldwide, including 2.3 million newborns, with 100,000 deaths directly due to severe acute malnutrition (MAS). Newborn deaths accounted for nearly half of under‑5 mortality, mainly from prematurity (36%) and intrapartum complications (21%), along with infections (neonatal sepsis) and congenital anomalies. Among ages 5–24, 2.1 million deaths occurred in 2024, with infectious diseases and injuries remaining the main causes; malaria alone accounted for 17% of deaths in this group, with most deaths in sub-Saharan Africa. Niger, Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Chad are heavily affected. Sub-Saharan Africa bore 58% of under‑5 deaths in 2024; South Asia 25%. Conflict and fragility triple the risk of death before age five. The report urges renewed political commitment, sustained investment in primary health care, and affordable interventions like vaccination and MAS treatment.

articles.headline: 4,9 Juta Anak di Dunia Tewas akibat Mal Nutrisi hingga Penyakit Menular
articles.headlineTranslated: 4.9 million children worldwide die from malnutrition and infectious diseases.
articles.summary: Nearly 4.9 million children under five died in 2024, including 2.3 million newborns. The report flags malnutrition and infectious diseases as the main drivers, with more than 100,000 deaths from severe acute malnutrition among 1 month–5 years. Nine major infections account for 43% of under-five deaths globally. In the first month of life, malaria, diarrhea, and pneumonia continue to kill in high-burden settings such as Chad, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Niger, and Nigeria. Neonatal deaths now account for almost half of all under-five fatalities, reflecting slower progress in preventing death around birth; prematurity and birth complications are major contributors alongside infections. Sub-Saharan Africa alone accounts for 58% of under-five deaths in 2024, while South Asia accounts for 25%. About 2.1 million deaths occur among ages 5–24. Ongoing funding cuts threaten maternal, newborn, and child health programs, with calls for renewed political commitment and stronger primary health care and data systems.

articles.headline: Puutiaiset heräsivät talvilevoltaan - Turun yliopisto pyytää punkkinäytteitä tutkittavaksi - SSS.fi
articles.headlineTranslated: Ticks woke from their winter sleep — University of Turku requests tick samples for analysis — SSS.fi.
articles.summary: Ticks wake from winter sleep as Finland enters the March active season; the University of Turku appeals for citizen mail-in tick samples to map nationwide changes in tick species and their pathogens. The citizen science effort builds on 2015 data that yielded nearly 20,000 ticks. Neoehrlichia mikurensis was among pathogens identified, with diagnostic testing established at Turku University Hospital in 2024, the same year Finland recorded its first human case linked to the bacterium. The first adult Hyalomma ticks—Mediterranean in origin, arriving via migratory birds—were found in Helsinki in 2024. Hyalomma is a known vector for Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever virus. Warmer summers allow these ticks to mature and spread pathogens. The ongoing study aims to chart shifts in tick distributions and pathogen presence across Finland, including implications for imported/exported cases.

articles.headline: Viruela de mono: "Hay varias formas de contagio, pero la mayoría son debido al sexo sin cuidado" - Primera Edición
articles.headlineTranslated: Monkeypox: "There are several modes of transmission, but most are due to unsafe sex" - First Edition.
articles.summary: First clade Ib mpox case detected in Argentina: a 31-year-old man from the City of Buenos Aires, with no travel history, treated outpatient and progressing favorably. In 2026 Argentina had five mpox cases, all clade II (four in Buenos Aires, one in Río Negro). Globally in 2026, mpox expanded in the Americas to 14 cases (USA 9, Canada 2, Brazil 2, Mexico 1, Argentina 1) with community transmission in France, Portugal, and Spain. Expert Hugo Pizzi characterized the Buenos Aires case as a minor genetic variation, not alarming, part of a broader cluster of about 70 cases in the country. He noted mpox originated in Africa (Zaire/DRC) in the 1970s, with transmission mainly via sexual contact, plus saliva, close contact, and contaminated bed linens. He emphasized prevention and sexual health awareness amid rising sexually transmitted infections.

articles.headline: Nueva cepa de viruela del mono, más  contagiosa, se expande por América; hay casos en México - El Heraldo de México
articles.headlineTranslated: New, more contagious strain of monkeypox spreading across the Americas; there are cases in Mexico.
articles.summary: New, more contagious monkeypox Clade Ib is spreading across the Americas; Argentina reports its first Mpox Clade Ib case in a 31-year-old Buenos Aires resident with no recent international travel; the patient is ambulatory and improving. Clade Ib, first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2023, is more transmissible than Clade II, which accounts for five Argentine cases. In 2026, Clade Ib cases have reached 14 in the Americas: 9 in the United States, 2 in Canada, 2 in Brazil, 1 in Mexico, 1 in Argentina. Transmission is via close contact or sexual contact; incubation 6–13 days; symptoms include painful skin/mucosal lesions (genital/anal), fever, fatigue, myalgias, headache, and lymphadenopathy. Isolation until crusts fall and skin heals; healthcare workers should use PPE, and contact tracing should begin within 24 hours with a 21-day monitoring period. A vaccinia-based vaccine exists; vaccination is prioritized for endemic zones and high-risk groups.

articles.headline: Mpox Clado Ib en Argentina: qué es, cómo se contagia y cuáles son los síntomas de la variante de la viruela símica
articles.headlineTranslated: Mpox Clade Ib in Argentina: What It Is, How It Spreads, and What Are the Symptoms of the Monkeypox Variant
articles.summary: Argentina confirms its first Mpox Clade Ib case. A 31-year-old man in Buenos Aires with no recent international travel is improving on outpatient care. Clade Ib, originating in the DRC in 2023, is more contagious and potentially more severe than the earlier Clade II; Argentina had five Clade II cases previously in the Buenos Aires area and Río Negro. Americas report 14 mpox cases, including the US, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina; Europe (France, Portugal, Spain) reports transmission. The Ministry urges heightened epidemiological surveillance to quickly identify suspects, especially those with umbilicated lesions, proctitis, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, or sore throat, and to assess travel history or contact with travelers from affected areas. Mpox, a zoonotic orthopoxvirus, transmits by close contact; incubation 5–21 days; symptoms include painful genital/anal lesions; isolation until crusts heal and new skin forms; PPE for health workers. Argentina lacks approved mpox vaccines; antivirals are not registered with ANMAT.

articles.summary: First case of Mpox Clade Ib confirmed in Argentina: a 31-year-old man in Buenos Aires, with no recent travel, was treated as an outpatient and is in good health with favorable evolution. articles.headline: Viruela del mono: Es una cepa más agresiva y con mayor riesgo de contagio
articles.headlineTranslated: Monkeypox: It is a more aggressive strain with a higher risk of contagion.
articles.summary: Argentina has detected a more aggressive, highly contagious clade of monkeypox, according to infectious disease expert Hugo Pizzi on Cadena 3 Rosario. The virus, first identified in the 1970s in the Democratic Republic of Congo, emerged in humans via close contact, including consumption of infected animals; it later spread from Africa to Europe. In Argentina, prior detections involved a less virulent variant, but current reports point to a more virulent clade with a higher mortality risk. Transmission is not limited to intimate contact; it can occur through saliva, sharing objects, or contact with contaminated surfaces, with the virus potentially persisting on sheets and other items. Incubation can extend to 21 days or more, hindering early detection. Vaccines developed in the United States and Europe have shown efficacy, though availability remains limited in some countries. Emphasis on personal preventive measures and reducing risky behaviors remains crucial.

articles.headline: Viruela del mono en la Argentina: cuáles son los síntomas de la variante Mpox Clado Ib
articles.headlineTranslated: Monkeypox in Argentina: what are the symptoms of the Mpox Clade Ib variant
articles.summary: Argentina confirmed its first mpox Clade Ib case: a 31-year-old man in Buenos Aires with no travel history, managed as an outpatient and progressing favorably. Clade Ib has drawn international surveillance due to higher transmissibility and distinctive clinical features since its detection in 2023. Mpox typically causes skin and mucosal lesions that can be genital/anal, oropharyngeal, or rectal; fever, fatigue, myalgias, headache, and lymphadenopathy, with incubation of five to 21 days (usually six to 13). The eruption usually begins on the face and spreads with lesions in the same stage within a region, often larger and deeper. In the South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak (Sept 2023–Jan 2024), 241 suspected cases all had exanthem; 59% fever, 42% adenopathy, 27% odynophagia, 18% genital lesions. Complications can include secondary bacterial skin infections and ocular, pulmonary, neurologic, and hepatic involvement as part of mpox’s spectrum.

The eruption usually begins on the face and spreads with lesions in the same stage within a region, often larger and deeper. In the South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak (Sept 2023–Jan 2024), 241 suspected cases all had exanthem; 59% fever, 42% adenopathy, 27% odynophagia, 18% genital lesions. Complications can include secondary bacterial skin infections and ocular, pulmonary, neurologic, and hepatic involvement as part of mpox’s spectrum.

articles.headline: Accords sanitaires Afrique-États-Unis : les alertes d'un virologue
articles.headlineTranslated: Africa-United States Health Agreements: The Virologist's Warnings
articles.summary: At the end of February 2026, the United States signed 18 bilateral health agreements with 18 African countries totaling $19.8 billion (US pledges $12.2B; recipient nations $7.5B). Participating states include Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, DRC, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Uganda. Virologist Oyewale Tomori warns that conditions demanding rapid sharing of sensitive health data and pathogen samples—potentially for up to 25 years—risk sovereignty and access to resulting vaccines and therapies. The deals propose five-year initial terms but raise concerns about 20+-year data/pathogen sharing; critics urge locally funded capacity building and data control. Zambia’s health agreement is linked to a separate mining-sector deal; Nigeria’s accord emphasizes promoting Christian health providers with about $200M for 900+ facilities, sparking inclusivity debates. The package aims nearly $2.1B for HIV, TB, malaria, maternal/child health, and polio, with Nigeria increasing national health expenditure by roughly 3 trillion naira.

articles.headline: Alarma sanitaria en Argentina: confirmaron el primer caso de una variante más contagiosa de viruela del mono
articles.headlineTranslated: Public health alert in Argentina: first case of a more contagious monkeypox variant confirmed.
articles.summary: Argentina confirms its first Monkeypox (Mpox) Clade Ib case, detected in a 31-year-old man in Buenos Aires City with no travel history; treated as an outpatient and recovering. Clade Ib, identified in late 2023 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, is more transmissible and virulent, linked to higher mortality and pediatric impact. By 2026, five mpox cases of Clade II had been confirmed in Argentina (four in Buenos Aires, one in Río Negro). Authorities urge reinforced surveillance as mpox spreads globally, with 14 cases in the Americas. For the index case, isolation is advised until crusts fall, and contact tracing within 24 hours with a 21-day follow-up. Transmission occurs mainly via direct contact with lesions or mucous membranes or with recently contaminated objects. Incubation is 5–21 days; disease is typically self-limiting over 14–21 days with symptomatic care. Prodromal symptoms may include fever, headache, myalgias, lymphadenopathy, asthenia, sore throat, and anorectal/genital pain.

articles.headline: Confirmaron el primer caso de viruela del mono de la variante más contagiosa en Argentina: cuáles son sus síntomas
articles.headlineTranslated: They confirmed the first case of the most contagious variant of monkeypox in Argentina: what are its symptoms.
articles.summary: Clade Ib, a newly identified mpox (monkeypox) variant detected in late 2023 in the Democratic Republic of Congo, shows higher transmissibility and virulence than prior strains. Authorities warn it can spread rapidly through sexual and community contact. In 2026, Argentina reported five mpox cases, all linked to Clade II, amid a shifting landscape as Clade Ib expands regionally. Reports of Clade Ib infections have surfaced in the United States, Canada, Brazil, and Mexico, with Argentina also affected; community transmission has been documented in France, Portugal, and Spain. Transmission occurs mainly via direct contact with skin or mucosal lesions in close or sexual contact; contaminated objects and prolonged exposure to respiratory secretions can also spread the virus. Incubation is 5–21 days, and illness is typically self-limited over 2–3 weeks. Early symptoms include fever, headache, muscle pains, swollen lymph nodes, fatigue, and sore throat, followed by lesions on the genital, anal, face, or limbs.
